subject: Cloud Computing
title: Encryption at Rest
description: A short lesson to help you apply Encryption at Rest.

hook.text: A hard drive is stolen from a data center. If the data is encrypted at rest, the thief gets nothing useful.

buildup.text: Encryption at rest scrambles stored data using a key. Without the key, the data is meaningless noise.

discovery.text: Most cloud providers encrypt all data at rest by default now. S3, Azure Blob, and GCS all do it.

twist.text: Default encryption uses provider-managed keys. You trust the provider not to misuse or lose them.

climax.text: For maximum control, use customer-managed keys. You own the key — the provider can't read your data.

punchline.text: Encrypted data at rest is useless to a thief. Keep the key safe.

quiz.question: What is the advantage of using customer-managed encryption keys?
options: You control the key, so even the cloud provider cannot read your data
Customer-managed keys are always free of charge
They encrypt data faster than provider-managed keys

details.summary: Encryption at rest protects stored data by encrypting it on disk so that even if physical storage is compromised, the data remains unreadable without the decryption key. All major cloud providers offer default or configurable encryption for storage services.
details.whyItMatters: Data theft from stolen disks or unauthorized access to storage is a real threat. Encryption at rest ensures data remains protected even when physical security fails.
takeaways: Data is encrypted on disk using symmetric keys
All major clouds offer default encryption at rest
Key management determines who can decrypt the data

faq.question: Should you use provider-managed or customer-managed keys?
faq.answer: Provider-managed keys are simpler but give you less control. Customer-managed keys let you control rotation, access policies, and revocation. For sensitive or regulated data, customer-managed keys are recommended to maintain full control over decryption.

faq.question: Does encryption at rest slow performance?
faq.answer: Modern cloud storage uses hardware-accelerated encryption with negligible performance impact. AES-256 encryption is performed by dedicated chips in storage controllers, making encrypted reads and writes virtually as fast as unencrypted ones.
